patients.summary: Retired postal worker with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity and untreated hyperlipidemia who joined the practice in 2021. From December 2024 he has three ED visits for decompensated heart failure; an echo shows LVEF 35%, and his home regimen of metformin, lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide never changes.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64 y/o man transferring care; his last PCP office is closing its adult panel and he wanted somewhere he could reach a doctor by phone. Retired from the postal service, was a letter carrier on a walking route for most of it.

PMH: HTN for roughly 12 years. T2DM for about 8 years, metformin only, never on insulin. Weight has been an issue since his 40s. Told his cholesterol was high a few years back, was never put on anything for it.
PSH: appendectomy at 22. Right knee scope at 54, no problems since.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg q AM. Brought the bottles; fills line up.
Allergies: sulfa antibiotics, rash years ago.
FH: father had an MI at 70, also HTN. Mother had T2DM and heart failure, died at 81. Brother with HTN and coronary disease.
SH: smoked about a pack a day for 25 years, stopped in 2016. Drinks maybe 1-2 times a month. Lives on his own, drives.
Vaccines: two Pfizer doses this spring at the pharmacy.

ROS: feels fine. No exertional chest discomfort, no breathlessness, no swelling, no polyuria, no foot numbness, no vision change.

Exam: BP 142/88 on recheck. BMI about 34. Well appearing. Fundi not dilated. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abd obese, soft, healed RLQ scar. No peripheral edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, DP and PT pulses 2+.

A/P
1. HTN: a bit above goal on lisinopril + HCTZ. Wants to work on salt first. Recheck next visit, no change today.
2. T2DM: A1c, CMP, urine albumin/creatinine today.
3. Obesity: talked about walking again, he used to cover miles a day.
4. Hyperlipidemia: lipid panel today.
5. Former smoker, 25 pk-yr, quit 2016: eligible for annual low-dose CT, ordered. One-time aortic ultrasound ordered.
6. HCV and HIV screening once, both drawn today.
7. Prior records requested. Colonoscopy he thinks was 2017.
RTC 6 months, sooner for BP if needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Yeager, your labs are back. Your A1c is 7.6, a little above where we'd like it, so let's see what more walking does before we think about another medicine. Kidney function and potassium are fine and there is no protein leaking into the urine. LDL cholesterol is 136. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative and never need repeating. Talk soon.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Received 14 pages from previous PCP office. Contents: medication list (metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily), allergy list (sulfa - rash), visit notes 2018-2021 for diabetes and BP, and a screening colonoscopy report from 2017: cecum reached, good prep, no polyps, recall 10 years. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records review

Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart normal in size. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

IPPE, within his first year of Medicare Part B (turned 65 last July).
Functional: independent, drives, does his own shopping. No falls. Hearing fine in conversation. Vision: eye exam in March, no retinopathy.
PHQ-2 0. Cognition: no concerns from him, recall 3/3.
Advance directive: none yet; handed him the health care proxy form, he will think about who to name.

Exam: BP and weight as charted, BMI about 34. Ears clear. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Extremities without edema. Foot exam: monofilament intact bilaterally, pulses palpable, no calluses.

Plan
- Labs: CMP, lipids, A1c, urine albumin/creatinine
- Shingrix #1 today, #2 in the fall
- LDCT due July
- Colonoscopy 2017 normal, due 2027
- Continue metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ

events.reason: Shortness of breath and leg swelling

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Small bilateral pleural effusions with blunting of both costophrenic angles. No focal consolidation. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Emergency Department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, area community hospital. Visit 2024-12-05.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
CC: short of breath walking, both legs swollen.
HPI: 68-year-old man, retired mail carrier, reports roughly two months of slowly worsening breathlessness with exertion and swelling of both lower legs. Denies chest pain, fevers and cough.
Hx: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity, hyperlipidemia. Appendectomy, R knee arthroscopy. Ex-smoker, 25 pack-years, quit 2016. Rare alcohol.
Home meds: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide.
Family: father MI at 70; mother diabetes and heart failure; brother HTN and CAD.
Triage vitals: BP 145/90, HR 88, RR 20.
Exam: JVD present. S3 gallop. Breath sounds reduced at both bases, no crackles. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin bilaterally.
CXR: small effusions on both sides.
Procedure: diagnostic thoracentesis performed in the department after consent, ultrasound guidance, without complication.
Pleural fluid: protein 1.5 g/dL (serum 6.8), LDH 110 U/L (serum 200), pH 7.45. Ratios consistent with a transudate.
ED impression: acute decompensated heart failure.
Disposition: discharged home, home medications unchanged. Follow up with primary care within one week; return for worsening breathing.

documents.title: ED record received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record from 12/5 received by fax, 6 pages. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Patient call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calls: was in the ER last night for trouble breathing and swollen legs, they took fluid off his lung and sent him home late. Told it was his heart. Breathing a little easier this morning, no chest pain. Booked with PCP Tuesday 12/10. Advised 911 if worse.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen in ED 12/5 with two months of exertional dyspnea and leg edema; I have the ED record. Small bilateral effusions, tap in the ED was transudative, impression decompensated HF. No new meds given. Since then: breathing better than that night, can do the stairs to the car slowly. Ankles still swell by evening. Sleeping flat. No chest pain.
O: Vitals as charted. No JVD visible sitting up. Heart regular, no gallop heard today. Lungs clear to bases. Trace to 1+ edema at the ankles bilaterally.
A/P:
1. Heart failure, new presentation. Need the EF - transthoracic echo ordered. BMP today.
2. HTN on lisinopril + HCTZ, continue.
3. T2DM on metformin, continue.
Daily weights; call for gain of more than 3 lb in a day or 5 in a week, or worse breathing. Back after the echo.

conditions.label: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

reports.text: Outpatient echo laboratory, outside cardiology group. Indication: heart failure. Allergies: sulfa. Complete 2D study with color flow and spectral analysis. Technically adequate images. Left ventricle mildly dilated with global hypokinesis; LVEF 35% by biplane method. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Atria normal in size. Aortic, mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves without significant stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal size.
reports.conclusion: Mildly dilated left ventricle with global hypokinesis, LVEF 35%. No significant valve disease. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Echo result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with echo: pumping function reduced, EF 35%, valves fine. Added HFrEF to his problem list. He asked if this is what his mother had; told him it sounds similar. Keep the daily weights going and come in mid-January. Questions answered.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
HFrEF f/u, echo 12/19 EF 35% with global hypokinesis.
S: Feels back to himself. Leg swelling gone for about two weeks. Home weights 241-244 lb, steady. Sleeps on one pillow. Walks the mall without stopping.
O: Vitals as charted. Neck veins flat. RRR, no S3. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P:
- The December decompensation has settled; taken off the active list. HFrEF remains.
- HTN, T2DM: continue metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ.
- BMP today.
- Keep weighing daily, low salt.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Emergency Department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, area community hospital. Date of service 2025-09-04.
Allergies: sulfa (rash).
Chief complaint: dyspnea, can't lie flat.
History: 69 y/o M with chronic HFrEF, seen here about nine months ago for the same, now with two weeks of increasing breathlessness on exertion and needing to sleep propped up. He also notes his belt has gotten tighter around the middle though he hasn't changed how he eats and his weight is the same.
PMH: HFrEF, HTN, T2DM, obesity, hyperlipidemia. PSH: appendectomy, R knee scope.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ.
SH: former smoker (25 pk-yr, quit 2016), occasional alcohol, retired postal worker.
FH: father MI at 70, HTN; mother DM2 and CHF, died 81; brother HTN, CAD.
Vitals: BP 150/90, P 102, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.
Exam: JVD. Crackles both lung fields. S3. Pitting edema both lower extremities.
Labs: BNP 900 pg/mL. Na 140, K 4.5, Cr 1.2. Glucose 160 (reported as fasting).
CXR: cardiomegaly, pulmonary vascular congestion.
ECG: LVH.
Impression: acute decompensated heart failure.
Disposition: discharged home on his home regimen; PCP follow-up.

documents.title: ED record received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Second request answered: ED record from 9/4 received, 5 pages. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record from 9/4 reviewed, matches what he described at his 9/10 visit. BNP 900, Cr 1.2, K 4.5. CXR congestion, ECG LVH.

documents.title: Was in the ER
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know I ended up in the ER again Thursday night. Couldn't breathe lying down for about two weeks and finally went in. Same thing as last December they said, heart. They let me go early Friday morning. Feeling better but tired. Do you want to see me?

documents.title: RE: Was in the ER
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know. The doctor wants to see you this week - you're booked for Wednesday 9/10 at 9:40. Please bring your weight log. If your breathing gets worse before then, call 911.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: ED visit 9/4 for two weeks of DOE and orthopnea; per his account told it was the heart again and sent home in the early morning on the same meds. No ED paperwork yet - records requested. Today breathing close to his usual, sleeping on two pillows. Some ankle swelling at night. Notes his waistband is snugger but the scale hasn't moved.
O: Vitals as charted, SpO2 95% RA. Faint crackles at the right base. Heart regular. 1+ ankle edema bilaterally.
A/P:
1. HFrEF (EF 35%) with a second decompensation by history. Back on the active list until settled.
2. BMP today.
3. Daily weights, salt limits reviewed with him again.
4. Continue metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ.
Recheck in about 10 weeks, sooner if needed.
